proof_summary: A hypergeometric telescoping identity first establishes a three-term recurrence, whose iterated \(2\times2\) transfer matrices yield the recurrence for every arithmetic subsequence after explicit common factors are removed. The remaining matrix-entry polynomial has alternating signs at consecutive half-integers, forcing all its roots into the required interval, while a reflection identity gives its symmetry; suitable rescaling and the even polynomial from a \(2m\)-step block then produce \(P\) and \(Q\) with the claimed root locations.
